sections.title: Form and flowers
sections.text: Italian senna is a low perennial herb or shrublet arising from a woody base, usually 15–60 cm tall, with spreading or ascending stems. Its pinnate leaves have several pairs of oval leaflets. Axillary racemes carry yellow to orange flowers; the flattened pods are about 2.5–6 cm long and 1.5–2 cm wide, with a raised ridge over each segment.

sections.title: Uses and caution
sections.text: Leaves have been used as a laxative and in traditional remedies, but reported chemistry and toxicity vary. A laboratory study of leaf extracts in rats does not establish safety for people. The sources consulted do not support a general food recommendation.
